st.headline: SoftBank junk bond sale raises stakes for CEO Son’s all-in AI bet
st.teaser: Those investments are coming under scrutiny about whether a payoff from the expenditures by AI companies will come soon enough.
fullText: TOKYO – SoftBank’s promise to pay its highest-ever yields in a record US$11 billion (S$14.1 billion) junk-bond offering highlights the pressure on CEO Masayoshi Son to secure returns on his all-in bet on AI amid concerns about possible overheating in the market.
The SoftBank debt issuance in September added to a sharp surge in corporate borrowing in 2026, including major bond sales from Amazon.com, Alphabet and Tencent.
The scale of Son’s investments, which include backing totalling US$64.6 billion for ChatGPT maker OpenAI, has made the technology-and-investing conglomerate a bellwether for AI sentiment.

Those fresh investments are now coming under sharper scrutiny by analysts and investors amid worries about the degree of concentration in SoftBank’s portfolio and whether a payoff from the expenditures by AI companies will come soon enough.

SoftBank previously sold shares in Nvidia and T-Mobile US to fund its investments, but it is now borrowing at record yields of up to 9.75% to retain assets that it believes will appreciate, a senior SoftBank executive told Reuters.

“We’ve borrowed money in large part because we don’t want to sell assets that we believe will keep rising in value,” said Alex Clavel, CEO of SoftBank Investment Advisers, which manages the Vision Funds.
Sam Altman’s OpenAI is the core investment in the latest iteration of Son’s investment strategy, following lucrative bets on Chinese tech giant Alibaba and chip designer Arm.
“Given OpenAI’s appreciation to date, 9.75% is still very reasonable,” Clavel said.

Arm’s valuation has grown fivefold since it floated in 2023 and further listings from SoftBank’s private AI portfolio would clarify their value and more easily allow the assets to be monetised for additional investment activity.

Altman has said OpenAI will not go public in 2026, citing safety concerns about artificial intelligence. It also faces competition from rival Anthropic and hyperscalers, as well as low-cost Chinese labs.
SoftBank was previously “betting on a bunch of numbers at the roulette table. Now it’s red or black, either lose everything or gain everything”, said analyst David Gibson of MST Financial.

SoftBank will pay its highest-ever coupon of 9.75% on a bond issued in September that matures in 2034. That return compares with Alphabet offering 5.2% for a bond issued in August that matures in 2033.

SoftBank’s shares surged to a record high of 8,632 yen in June, though they have fallen 38% since then, while its credit default swap spreads – the cost to insure its debt against a default or other credit event – jumped 24% over the same period.
SoftBank’s higher yields reflect investor perceptions of their risk and concentration in large positions, analysts say.
“The bets are much bigger than we’ve ever seen,” said Amir Anvarzadeh of Asymmetric Advisors, who recommends shorting the stock.
James Athey, a fixed-income portfolio manager at Marlborough, said the fund was not allocating to high-yield bonds at this stage of the credit cycle, given current tight spread levels.
“SoftBank is so aggressive, so concentrated and so all-in, I don’t think we’d be looking there first anyway,” he said.
Clavel, however, says SoftBank’s OpenAI backing reflects their deep business ties.
“We see OpenAI as a partner, building a relationship that can deliver strategic value as well as financial returns,” he said.
OpenAI is also an investor in and customer of data centre company SB Energy, which SoftBank is looking to list and may seek a valuation of US$50 billion, Reuters has reported.

“SoftBank is taking advantage of hyper-excitement around AI-driven businesses, applying very high valuations for relatively low revenues, and they are looking to capitalise,” said MST’s Gibson of the potential valuation.
Son’s bets have a mixed track record – his investment in Chinese tech giant Alibaba was a major success, but Son also directed US$16 billion to Adam Neumann’s WeWork, which ultimately went bankrupt.
Other setbacks included a crash in the value of its investments as central banks moved to hike rates in 2022.
“OpenAI’s value appreciation to date far exceeds the losses in our 2021 vintage investments,” Clavel said.
Over the decades, Son has navigated market peaks and troughs to build SoftBank into a 30 trillion yen (S$242 billion) company.
“Being priced in is a massive transformation of the workplace with AI effectively taking over a big chunk of what gets done with human brains,” said Morningstar senior equity analyst Dan Baker.
“If that goes ahead, it’s hard to see their investments not being very successful,” he said. REUTERS

cna.headline: PSG boss Luis Enrique hopes Man City are not stripped of titles
cna.teaser: PSG boss Luis Enrique hopes Man City are not stripped of titles
fullText: Oct 14 : Paris St Germain boss Luis Enrique said Manchester City were deserving winners of their trophies and should be allowed to keep them, despite the English club facing sanctions after being found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules.
The Premier League said ​City had used "sham" commercial contracts as part of schemes to inflate revenue and understate costs by more than £900 million ($1.19 billion).

City, who have denied wrongdoing throughout the case and have appealed the verdict, could face punishments ranging from fines and a points deduction, to relegation and potentially being stripped of their titles.

Asked about the verdict before PSG's Champions League match against City, Luis Enrique told a press conference on Tuesday: "The first thing when you hear that, it's a surprise, but I think we need to respect the process and wait for the final decision.

"I love the way they play football, and after that, you have to wait (for the) last decision and nothing else ... I think the trophies that you win on the pitch remains on the pitch, and they deserve to win that. I hope they can avoid that sanction."
City host PSG at the Etihad Stadium later on Wednesday.
A single handpicked story that we think you shouldn't miss. Just one a day.

Officials emphasize that accessible infrastructure is essential to overcoming range anxiety among prospective buyers.

economistArticle.title: How to Lose Money Betting Against Europe
paras: Short-selling European sovereign debt has long been regarded as a tempting trade for global macro hedge funds. When political friction flares up between Brussels and national capitals, market yields frequently surge as nervous investors price in fiscal disintegration. Yet, those who position themselves for an imminent monetary collapse invariably discover that betting against European cohesion is a perilous endeavor.

The fundamental flaw in the bear thesis lies in underestimating the institutional firepower of the European Central Bank. While national politicians may trade accusatory rhetoric during public summits, the central bank possesses an unyielding mandate to safeguard the single currency. Through backstop programs and flexible bond-buying mechanisms, policymakers can effectively cap borrowing spreads before market distress becomes systemic.

Moreover, sovereign crisis dynamics in Europe rarely follow a purely linear narrative driven by budget deficits. Political resolve often hardens precisely when existential threats loom largest over the monetary union. Member states that appear fractious during quiet periods historically demonstrate a remarkable capacity for compromise when default risks jeopardize their banking sectors.

Investors who rely solely on fiscal metrics without accounting for institutional emergency mechanisms frequently miscalculate their timing. While political squabbles will inevitably trigger short-term market volatility, the underlying commitment to European economic integration remains formidable. Those seeking quick profits from Europe's structural fragilities often end up paying a heavy toll.
economistArticle.cn:
卖空欧洲主权债务长期以来一直被全球宏观对冲基金视为极具诱惑力的交易。当布鲁塞尔与各成员国首都之间爆发政治摩擦时，随着不安的投资者将财政解体的风险计入价格，市场收益率往往会大幅飙升。然而，那些做空欧洲并预判其货币体系即刻崩溃的人，无一例外地发现，押注欧洲内部凝聚力的破裂是一项极其危险的举动。

看空论调的根本缺陷在于低估了欧洲中央银行的制度威慑力。尽管各国政治家可能会在公开峰会上互相指责，但央行拥有维护单一货币的坚定授权。通过后备计划和灵活的债券购买机制，政策制定者可以在市场动荡演变成系统性危机之前，有效地限制借贷利差的扩大。

此外，欧洲主权危机的演变机制很少遵循由预算赤字所主导的简单线性逻辑。每当生存威胁笼罩单一货币联盟时，政治决心往往反而会强化。在平静时期显得分歧严重的成员国，历来证明了当违约风险危及其银行体系时，它们拥有非凡的妥协能力。

仅仅依赖财政指标而忽视制度性应急机制的投资者，常常会错判 timing。尽管政治争端不可避免地会引发短期市场波动，但欧洲经济一体化的底层承诺依然坚如磐石。企图从欧洲结构性脆弱中牟取暴利的投机者，最终往往付出高昂的代价。
